strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple models (GPT-5, Gemini, Claude, Qwen, DeepSeek) and datasets (IMO-GradingBench, Hard2Verify, QiuZhen-Bench) with consistent results
Clear demonstration that pessimistic verification outperforms majority voting for error detection, with better token efficiency than long-CoT scaling
Transparent about trade-offs (TPR decrease) and attempts to explain via dataset annotation analysis
Good presentation with clear figures (Figure 1 and 6) effectively showing efficiency-performance tradeoffs
Contributions of systematic comparison of verification strategies and new high-difficulty dataset (QiuZhen-Bench)
Honest discussion of limitations and case studies showing real instances of disagreement between verifiers and dataset labels
weaknesses: Limited novelty: builds on Liu et al. (2025) with straightforward combinations (simple/vertical/progressive verification); core variants lack fundamental innovation, making this primarily an empirical validation study rather than methodological advance

Insufficient evidence for key claim that 'most false negatives are dataset errors': manual review of only 15-20 cases per model (Table 1) is too small to support extrapolation to widespread mislabeling conclusion
Circular reasoning with QiuZhen-Bench: uses GPT-5 with progressive verification for labeling, then tests the method on the same benchmark, risking that systematic biases get baked into the benchmark
Missing theoretical justification: no formal analysis of why pessimistic verification should outperform majority voting, when it should be preferred, or what conditions enable its effectiveness

Confounded experimental design: different prompts used for different verification types (single-pass vs. chunk verification); ablation studies missing to isolate prompt quality effects from method effects
Manual case review focuses only on false negatives; misses analysis of false positives and true cases, providing incomplete picture of where verifier-annotation disagreements actually occur
Overclaiming in places (e.g., 'state-of-the-art models approach near human experts') without sufficient support
Reproducibility limitations: depends on proprietary models (GPT-5, Gemini) and QiuZhen-Bench construction via GPT-5 labeling creates non-reproducible benchmark without access to GPT-5

strengths: Clear practical contribution showing consistent improvements in error detection (TNR) across multiple models and datasets
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning 9 diverse models and multiple benchmarks with careful efficiency analysis
Honest discussion of dataset annotation issues and limitations, raising important quality concerns
Efficiency gains over long-CoT demonstrated in Figure 1 with significantly fewer equivalent output tokens
Well-structured presentation with effective visualizations and clear methodology
Reproducibility commitment with promised code and dataset release
weaknesses: Limited novelty: explicitly builds on Liu et al. (2025) with only natural extensions of three variants; primarily empirical validation
Insufficient evidence for central claim about annotation errors: only 13-20 manual cases per model reviewed without inter-rater reliability study
Circular validation on QiuZhen-Bench: ground truth labeled by GPT-5 progressive@3/6, the same method being evaluated; not discussed as limitation
No statistical rigor: missing confidence intervals, significance tests, ablation studies, or variance reporting on key results
Inadequate baseline comparisons: only single-pass verification and majority voting; lacks comparison to other ensemble or verification methods
Unexplored TPR-TNR trade-off: significant TPR decreases visible (especially in Figure 6) but no discussion of when this is acceptable for different applications
Missing theoretical justification: unclear why pessimistic outperforms majority voting formally or under what conditions it fails
Dense presentation of results: Figure 6 with 9 models per dataset difficult to parse; critical prompts relegated to appendix

strengths: Clear identification and articulation of error detection as the key verification bottleneck, well-motivated by recent work
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (IMO-GradingBench, Hard2Verify, QiuZhen-Bench) with consistent scaling trends
Significant practical efficiency gains (4× token savings for progressive vs. simple pessimistic verification) validated on state-of-the-art models
Honest and systematic case study analysis revealing annotation errors in established benchmarks (Section 3.4), with detailed examples and discussion
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 1), detailed reproducibility information (prompts, hyperparameters), and promised code release
Validation on real contest problems (IMO 2025, MathArena Apex 2025) demonstrating practical applicability beyond synthetic benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core concept (reject if any verifier finds error) is straightforward; variants are largely combinations of existing ideas without theoretical justification

Weak problem-solving validation: small benchmark sizes (6 IMO, 12 MathArena problems), modest absolute improvements (13→22 on 42 points), high variance in results (Figure 7), no statistical significance testing

Dataset annotation error analysis raises more concerns than it resolves: only 20 FN cases per model, subjective classification scheme without inter-rater reliability, circular reasoning risk (using strong model disagreement to 'correct' benchmarks), could bias evaluation in favor of frontier models

QiuZhen-Bench methodology problematic: GPT-5 used for both generation and annotation creating systematic bias, no human verification, only tested on smaller models, introduces new dataset with different distribution complicating interpretation
Missing systematic hyperparameter analysis: prog@3/6 chosen empirically for 'balanced performance' without sensitivity studies; no principled method for selecting n/k for new problems

Incomplete baseline comparisons: long CoT comparison constrained by model capabilities (can't adjust Qwen reasoning_effort), majority voting dismissed quickly, potential unfairness in comparison setup
Limited theoretical grounding: no analysis of why pessimistic verification reduces error rates, no complexity analysis, no formal justification for the approach
High reproducibility barriers: requires expensive access to frontier models and ability to reproduce GPT-5 annotations on custom dataset
